What does an 8-year UPSC journey actually look like?

AIR 100 Sattwik Satyakam Devta sits down with LevelUp IAS to talk about the attempts, setbacks, decisions and lessons that shaped his journey from starting UPSC preparation in 2018 to securing AIR 100.

From leaving a job at Maruti Suzuki to preparing alongside his NABARD career, Sattwik shares what changed in his final attempt, how he approached answer writing and revision, how he used AI, and why he stopped believing that preparation means cutting yourself off from everything else.

A candid conversation about preparing for UPSC with more clarity, balance and perspective.

Stationary waves in air columns is a fundamental chapter in Class 11 Physics that explains how sound waves behave in confined spaces. This comprehensive tutorial covers all essential concepts required for Intermediate (FSc Part 1) students following the FBISE, Punjab Board, and National Curriculum of Pakistan.

In this video, you will learn:
- What stationary waves (standing waves) are and how they form
- The difference between travelling waves and stationary waves
- Modes of vibration in open and closed air columns
- Resonance and resonance frequency concepts
- Practical applications using resonance tubes
- Calculation of wavelength and frequency in air columns
- Harmonics and overtones in musical instruments

Stationary waves in air columns are crucial for understanding acoustics, musical instruments, and sound propagation. This topic appears in all major examination boards including FBISE Federal Board, BISE Lahore, BISE Rawalpindi, BISE Multan, BISE Karachi, and other Punjab and provincial boards. It's an important chapter for class tests, midterms, and final board exams.

Whether you're a student preparing for FSc exams, a parent helping with homework, or a teacher looking for classroom resources, this video breaks down complex concepts into easy-to-understand explanations with clear diagrams and solved examples.

Don't forget to like this video, subscribe to the channel for more Class 11 and Class 12 Physics tutorials, and comment below with any questions or topics you'd like us to cover next.

Class 10 Maths Chapter 3 Review Exercise 3 covers transpose, determinant, adjoint and inverse of matrices - essential topics for Matric students preparing for FBISE, Punjab boards, and other examination bodies across Pakistan.

In this comprehensive video, we walk through every concept and solved example in Review Exercise 3, helping you master matrix operations that appear regularly in Matric final exams. Whether you follow the PCTB textbook, Sindh Board, or any other Pakistani curriculum, these fundamental matrix concepts are crucial for your mathematics foundation.

What You'll Learn:
- How to find the transpose of a matrix
- Calculating determinants of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices
- Finding the adjoint (adjugate) of a matrix
- Computing the inverse of a matrix using adjoint and determinant
- Solving Review Exercise 3 problems step-by-step
- Essential tricks and shortcuts for matrix calculations

These matrix concepts form the backbone of Class 10 algebra and are important for students planning to take Intermediate (FSc, ICS, I.Com) mathematics. Clear understanding now will make advanced linear algebra much easier.

Perfect for:
- Matric students (Class 10) studying under FBISE, Punjab boards, Sindh boards, KPK boards, or any Pakistani curriculum
- Students preparing for half-yearly and final exams
- Parents helping their children with homework
- Teachers looking for classroom teaching resources

Watch this video carefully, solve the problems along with us, and don't hesitate to rewind difficult parts. If you found this helpful, please like, subscribe, and comment with any questions or topics you'd like us to cover next.

One Program for Your Entire UPSC Preparation | GS Foundation for UPSC CSE 2028

Preparing for UPSC CSE 2028 as a beginner can often mean trying to figure out multiple courses for GS, Prelims, Mains, CSAT, Essay, Current Affairs, Answer Writing and Interview preparation.

The LevelUp IAS GS Foundation Course for UPSC CSE 2028 is designed as an integrated preparation system where these components are brought together under one program. The course covers GS Paper 1–4, Prelims and Mains preparation, CSAT, Essay, Current Affairs, Answer Writing, regular tests, revision, dedicated mentorship and Interview preparation.

In this short, Santosh Kumar Sir, Academic Director & Strategy Mentor at LevelUp IAS, explains the idea behind an integrated GS Foundation program: instead of continuously adding separate foundation, current affairs and test courses, aspirants can follow one structured system covering the major stages of UPSC preparation.

The program includes 1000+ hours of GS classes, weekly/monthly/quarterly/half-yearly Prelims and Mains tests, a 15-month Current Affairs pipeline, dedicated 1-to-1 mentorship, daily answer-writing practice, CSAT, Essay, intensive Prelims and Mains preparation, and an Interview Program.

The objective is not to promise selection, but to provide a structured and comprehensive preparation system that a serious aspirant can follow systematically for UPSC CSE 2028.
